raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Speed up the direct symmetric-memory DCP Output/LSE consumer introduced in
#50484. Publication, signaling, allocation, and buffer lifetimes stay unchanged;
this is a focused follow-up from our Shared-DCP work in #50009.

```text
ASIS
publish O/LSE -> signal -> one CTA per head
                          serial peer waits + shared weights -> final O

PR
publish O/LSE -> signal -> four independent warp/head consumers per CTA
                          parallel peer waits + vector loads -> final O
```

## Claims

- On 4x GB200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 c1 TPOT improved by 2.27% and output throughput
  by 2.07% across two matched fresh-process pairs. c32 serving was neutral.
- Complete direct Output/LSE operator latency improved by 32.4%-40.7% across
  the tested GLM decode shapes, including publication and synchronization.
- No new workspace, communication phase, or runtime option. Dispatch uses the
  warp consumer for SM100-family GPUs, a 512-element value dimension, and at
  most 32 peers. Other devices/layouts retain the existing consumer.

## Validation

### Output/LSE operator: 32.4%-40.7% lower latency

Complete operator timing includes publication and synchronization, not just the
consumer kernel. On 4x GB200: BF16 O, FP32 LSE, 64 total heads, D=512, DCP4.
Mean of three process medians; seven timing trials per process, maximum-rank
CUDA-graph latency.

| Rows | Base | PR | Latency reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 17.162 us | 11.143 us | 35.07% |
| 8 | 17.162 us | 11.276 us | 34.30% |
| 32 | 18.951 us | 12.569 us | 33.68% |
| 64 | 22.021 us | 14.883 us | 32.42% |
| 128 | 36.527 us | 21.672 us | 40.67% |

Candidate process CV was 0.015%-0.053% across the full row sweep. These are
operator improvements, not end-to-end serving gains.

### Serving: 2.27% lower c1 TPOT; c32 neutral

GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4/DCP4/EP4, FlashInfer sparse MLA, FP8 KV, 3072 input tokens,
128 output tokens, prefix caching disabled, 1800 MHz SM clocks. Each process
used 8 counted c1 requests and 128 counted c32 requests after warmup.

| Load | Base TPOT | PR TPOT | Base throughput | PR throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c1 | 19.552 ms | 19.109 ms | 46.576 tok/s | 47.538 tok/s |
| c32 | 81.386 ms | 81.386 ms | 340.973 tok/s | 340.987 tok/s |

c1 TPOT improved by 2.09% and 2.44% in the two pairs; candidate process CV was
0.19%. c1 p99 ITL improved by 3.49%. Mean TTFT changed by +0.27% at c1 and
-0.06% at c32; c32 p99 ITL changed by +0.13%. These small TTFT/c32 differences
are not claimed as improvements.

**Serving validation scope:** both arms use the same pinned model runtime
`71323cbf1a` (including the merged #54908 prefill correctness fix), with only
the stable-ABI Output/LSE operator rebuilt from base `d61081dc3d` or this PR.
This is a matched kernel A/B in an integrated model, not a full current-main
model-build validation. MRV2 uses FULL_DECODE_ONLY/breakable CUDA graphs with
compilation disabled. Both arms use the same explicit FlashInfer workspace
size and disabled FlashInfer all-reduce/JIT-autotune settings.

- Distributed test: 4 passed on DCP2/DCP4, covering FP16/BF16, both LSE bases,
  empty shards, padded strides, partial CTAs, both workspace slots, and
  changing-input CUDA-graph replay. Wired into the existing two-B200 CI job.
- Same 32-question GSM8K smoke with prompts padded to 3072 tokens: baseline
  28/32 and 26/32; candidate 29/32 and 30/32. All returned finite logprobs.
  This is a small smoke test, not a full accuracy or bitwise-equivalence claim.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed. The contributed benchmark also passed
  a four-GPU smoke run.

<details>
<summary>Operator reproduction and additional scope</summary>

Six-head-per-rank correctness/performance checks also passed. The comparison is against the native
upstream implementation; our historical three-kernel prototype is still faster
at some small shapes and is not replaced by this PR.

Run on base and candidate builds with exclusive GPU ownership:

```bash
pytest -q tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py \
  -k test_distributed_direct_a2a_matches_reference
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dcp_a2a_lse_reduce.py \
  --heads 64 --rows 1,8,16,24,31,32,64,128 --output result.json
```

Repeat the benchmark in three fresh processes. The integrated serving A/B uses
the pinned runtime and operator-substitution scope stated above. Setup failures
and the superseded row-cutoff variant are excluded from these measurements.

</details>

## Details

Each warp handles one output head. Lanes load peer readiness/LSE in parallel,
then combine aligned 16-byte payloads in FP32 registers. Four heads share a CTA,
removing the consumer's shared-weight staging and CTA-wide barrier. Final output
still waits for every contributing peer. Zero-weight payloads remain unread,
preserving empty-shard handling and fail-closed timeout behavior.

This does not duplicate #48196's project-before-merge/helix transport changes.
It changes neither the reduction's mathematical contract nor its transport, and
does not include Query, Top-K, Indexer, or generic Shared-DCP framework changes.
The test fixture also keeps query boundaries explicitly int32, as required by
the existing operator API.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Consumer-only change; existing ownership and synchronization.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Distributed tests, repeated units, model smoke,
  matched serving A/B, and CI wiring; validation limitations stated above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable checks pass.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Claims, controls, variability, and scope documented.

</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark the complete direct DCP Output/LSE operation under CUDA graphs.
+
+Example:
+    torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dcp_a2a_lse_reduce.py \
+        --heads 64 --rows 1,8,32,64,128 --output result.json
+Run unchanged on the base and candidate revisions, with exclusive GPU ownership.
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.dcp import DirectDCPA2AWorkspace
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=64)
+    parser.add_argument("--rows", default="1,8,32,64,128")
+    parser.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=7)
+    parser.add_argument("--replays", type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument("--unroll", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    rows = [int(value) for value in args.rows.split(",")]
+    if min(rows) <= 0 or min(args.trials, args.replays, args.unroll) <= 0:
+        parser.error("rows and timing counts must be positive")
+    device = torch.device("cuda", int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=device)
+    try:
+        world, rank = dist.get_world_size(), dist.get_rank()
+        if world <= 1 or args.heads <= 0 or args.heads % world:
+            raise ValueError("heads must divide evenly across multiple DCP ranks")
+        workspace = DirectDCPA2AWorkspace(
+            dist.group.WORLD,
+            device,
+            max(rows),
+            args.heads // world,
+            512,
+            torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        records = []
+        for num_rows in rows:
+            torch.manual_seed(100 + rank)
+            partial_output = torch.randn(
+                num_rows, args.heads, 512, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+            )
+            partial_lse = torch.randn(num_rows, args.heads, device=device)
+            workspace.lse_reduce(partial_output, partial_lse, False)
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            dist.barrier()
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                for _ in range(args.unroll):
+                    workspace.lse_reduce(partial_output, partial_lse, False)
+            for _ in range(10):
+                graph.replay()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            samples = []
+            for _ in range(args.trials):
+                dist.barrier()
+                start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                start.record()
+                for _ in range(args.replays):
+                    graph.replay()
+                end.record()
+                end.synchronize()
+                elapsed = torch.tensor(
+                    start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / (args.replays * args.unroll),
+                    device=device,
+                )
+                dist.all_reduce(elapsed, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX)
+                samples.append(elapsed.item())
+            record = {
+                "rows": num_rows,
+                "median_us": statistics.median(samples),
+                "samples_us": samples,
+            }
+            records.append(record)
+            if rank == 0:
+                print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
+        if rank == 0 and args.output:
+            args.output.write_text(
+                json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "world_size": world,
+                        "heads": args.heads,
+                        "head_dim": 512,
+                        "torch_version": torch.__version__,
+                        "trials": args.trials,
+                        "replays": args.replays,
+                        "unroll": args.unroll,
+                        "records": records,
+                    },
+                    indent=2,
+                )
+            )
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

             graph.replay()
         torch.accelerator.synchronize()

+    "heads_per_rank,dtype_name,is_base_e",
+    [(6, "bfloat16", False), (16, "float16", True)],
+)
+def test_distributed_direct_a2a_matches_reference(
+    world_size: int, heads_per_rank: int, dtype_name: str, is_base_e: bool
+):
     _distributed_run(
         _distributed_direct_a2a_worker,

-            "TEST_DTYPE": "bfloat16",
+            "TEST_DTYPE": dtype_name,

-            "LSE_BASE_E": "0",
+            "LSE_BASE_E": str(int(is_base_e)),
+            "TEST_HEADS_PER_RANK": str(heads_per_rank),
         },
     )
